skill.name: vibestart
skill.description: Guide TypeScript project creation and maintenance through the vibestart CLI. Discover stacks, preview changes, add capabilities, diagnose configuration, and upgrade templates while reviewing conflicts and manual changes.
skill.summary: Create and maintain vibestart TypeScript projects with preview-first CLI workflows.
skill.author: vinkydev

security_audit.summary: Ten detections are false positives involving Markdown or ordinary project workflows; six describe commands that fetch and execute an unpinned npm package. Broad rollback instructions can discard unrelated edits and delete untracked files created after the operation starts. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious exfiltration in the reviewed skill files; external package implementation was not available.

remediation.issue: Discovery and help commands execute an unpinned npm package with automatic installation approval.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicitly approved exact CLI version for discovery, help, previews, and writes; disclose registry access and execution before the first invocation.

remediation.issue: Rollback instructions restore all tracked files and delete untracked files without checking for new unrelated work.
remediation.suggestion: Replace blanket rollback with operation-specific restoration; review the deletion preview and obtain explicit approval before deleting untracked files.

content.user_title: Create and Maintain VibeStart TypeScript Projects
content.value_statement: Project scaffolding and template upgrades require consistent choices and careful review of existing code. This skill guides vibestart CLI discovery, previews, capability additions, and maintenance.
actual_capabilities: Guide live discovery of supported stacks, recipes, and valid project choices through CLI help and structured listings.
Preview project creation and distinguish package-manager choices from Hono runtime choices.
Guide preview and application of supported Knip, Ultracite, and Docker capability additions.
Interpret read-only doctor results, including offline limitations and configuration issues.
Guide version-pinned template upgrades, conflict resolution, and manual porting of starter source changes.
Report operation status, checks actually run, deferred installation, and remaining work.
limitations: Installing the skill does not install the CLI, Vite+, or project dependencies.
Capability additions are not framework, database, runtime, or package-manager migrations.
Doctor results and successful previews do not prove that application tests passed.
CLI launchers may require registry access; writes can run dependency setup, project checks, services, or browsers.

use_cases.title: Start a TypeScript Application
use_cases.description: Discover supported stack choices and preview a new project before creating files and installing dependencies.

use_cases.title: Add Project Tooling
use_cases.description: Preview supported Knip, Ultracite, or Docker additions while preserving project choices and reviewing resulting changes.

use_cases.title: Review Template Upgrades
use_cases.description: Diagnose maintenance state, preview an exact target release, and identify conflicts, manual changes, and required validation.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Inspect Project State
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my vibestart project at [directory]. Use an approved CLI version, run offline diagnostics, and report configuration issues without applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Preview a New Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview a TypeScript project at [destination] using [requirements]. Discover supported choices, ask about missing decisions, and do not create files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Add Capabilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Knip and Ultracite to [directory]. Pin an approved CLI version, preview changes, preserve unrelated work, and apply only the requested additions.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Upgrade and Resolve Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade [directory] to [exact version]. Preview changes, preserve business edits, resolve conflicts, review manual source changes, and report checks and remaining work.
prompt_templates.scenario: Template upgrade with conflict and manual change review

output_examples.input: Preview a new TypeScript project without writing files.
output: Illustrative result: The selected stack is supported and the creation plan is ready for review.
No project files were written. Dependency installation and application validation were not run.
Next action: Review the destination, resolved choices, and file list before requesting creation.

output_examples.input: Explain a maintenance result that reports needs-install.
output: Project files were written, but dependency installation and validation remain unfinished.
An exit code of zero does not mean the project checks passed.
Next action: Follow the returned installation and check steps, then review conflicts and manual changes.

output_examples.input: Explain an upgrade result containing manual source changes.
output: The CLI reports template changes for project-owned source files but does not write those files.
Compare the previous and target template content, then adapt the relevant changes to the existing application.
Report each manual change as applied or deliberately declined, and list the validation actually completed.

best_practices: Approve and pin an exact CLI version before discovery, preview, or application; review external installation requirements.
Preview requested changes and start maintenance writes from a clean worktree without discarding unrelated edits.
Review conflicts and manual entries, then report only installation and validation steps that actually completed.
anti_patterns: Do not apply a preview when the user requested inspection only.
Do not hand-edit the project record or use creation to migrate an existing project.
Do not use blanket rollback commands without reviewing affected files and obtaining approval for deletions.

faq.question: Does installing this skill install the required tools?
faq.answer: No. The CLI, Vite+, and project dependencies require separate installation or invocation within your approved environment.

faq.question: Can I inspect a project without applying changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Doctor is read-only, and creation or maintenance previews avoid applying project changes. The npm launcher can still require registry access.

faq.question: Which capabilities can I add?
faq.answer: The references list Knip, Ultracite, and Docker. Check the live capability list for the approved CLI release.

faq.question: Will an upgrade replace my application code?
faq.answer: Upgrades merge supported configuration and dependency files. Project-owned source changes appear as manual entries for review, and conflicts require resolution.

faq.question: Does a successful result mean all tests passed?
faq.answer: No. Previews and doctor results do not validate application behavior. Deferred installation is unfinished even when the exit code is zero.

faq.question: Can adding capabilities change my framework or database?
faq.answer: No. The add workflow is not a framework, database, runtime, or package-manager migration. Use it only for supported capability additions.
